title: A first look at ozone and temperature
text:
PROJECT 01 / DATA VISUALIZATION




A short exploratory story using R’s built-in dataset to be replaced or expanded into a more thoughtful public data example.



Data New York air quality observations, May-September 1973


Question How do observed ozone levels vary with temperature?


Tools R / base datasets package




The built-in dataset records daily ozone, solar radiation, wind, and temperature measurements over five months. Here, we look at whether higher recorded temperatures tend to coincide with higher recorded ozone levels.





Code
air_quality <- datasets::airquality
observed <- air_quality[complete.cases(air_quality[, c("Ozone", "Temp")]), ]
month_colors <- c("#147565", "#d45c43", "#91a833", "#3e6e9a", "#b67e28")
observed$Month <- factor(observed$Month, levels = 5:9, labels = month.abb[5:9])

ggplot2::ggplot(observed, ggplot2::aes(x = Temp, y = Ozone, fill = Month)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(shape = 21, color = "white", size = 2.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(
    ggplot2::aes(x = Temp, y = Ozone, group = 1), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE, color = "#d45c43", linewidth = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = stats::setNames(month_colors, month.abb[5:9]),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Temperature (F)", y = "Ozone (ppb)") +
  ggplot2::theme_classic() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(color = "#53645f"),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(color = "#293a35"),
    legend.position = c(0.08, 0.96),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.background = ggplot2::element_blank()
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 2))








Figure 1: Observed ozone measurements tend to be higher on warmer days in this sample. The fitted line is descriptive, not causal.





The points suggest a positive association in these observations.



This is a small, single-location sample from 1973, spanning only May through September. Ozone values are missing on many days, and other factors such as solar radiation and wind also vary. This plot does not establish that temperature alone explains ozone changes or support a current air-quality conclusion.

Exploratory layout prototype only. No client engagement or business impact is represented.
